title_en: Why Oil Prices Are Surging Despite Recovering Supply
title_zh: Daan Struyven(Goldman Sachs):油价为何在供应回升之际依然飙升
subtitle_zh: Goldman Sachs Daan Struyven 解析风险溢价如何推高油价、运费、柴油、欧洲天然气与铜价,并坚持看好黄金。
summary_zh: 本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 由 Allison Nathan 对话 Goldman Sachs 全球大宗商品研究联席主管、石油研究主管 Daan Struyven，解析中东原油流量回升（波斯湾出口已达 2025 年均值的 100%–110%）之际油价为何仍飙升。Struyven 指出 Brent 已涨至约每桶 112 美元，源于中东紧张、供应下行风险加大：实物买家（炼厂）预防性抢桶，金融端因债股对油价敏感而大量对冲。他强调本月原油市场其实均衡（产量等于需求），公允价值约每桶 85 美元，近几周涨幅几乎全部来自约每桶 27 美元的风险溢价（risk premium）扩大，而非公允价值上升；基准预测今年底 Brent 90、2027 年均价 80，风险偏上行，若中期选举后无重大升级则风险溢价可能挤出。成品油是另一番景象：柴油出口仅为 2025 年均值 40%，叠加油轮运费过去一年飙升每桶 20 美元（约四分之三来自供应链重组），柴油趋紧正传导至汽油。欧洲天然气净上行风险显著——中东 LNG 出口仅约三分之一、库存低，TTF 或从约 90 欧元升至三位数甚至 150 欧元，但因需求已失约 20%、非中东供应上升，不会重演 2022 年 300 欧元峰值。他还看好铜（美中争夺有限金属，明年底前再涨约 10%）与黄金（央行购金速度是 2022 年前的 5 倍）。
description: Why Oil Prices Are Surging Despite Recovering Supply

turns.en: Oil flows from the Middle East have rebounded sharply, but prices remain high and rise it. So, what's keeping the market on edge? I'm Allison Nathan and this is Goldman Sachs Exchanges.
turns.zh: 中东的石油流量已经大幅回升,但油价仍然高企,还在往上走。那么,是什么让市场持续紧绷?我是 Allison Nathan,这里是 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。

turns.en: Joining me is Don Streven, co-head of Global Commodities Research and head of oil research at Goldman Sachs. Don, thanks for joining us again.
turns.zh: 与我对话的是 Daan Struyven,Goldman Sachs 全球大宗商品研究联席主管、石油研究主管。Daan,欢迎再次来到节目。

turns.en: You've been on the show a lot, but look, oil has been very topical, so thanks for joining us again. Thanks. As I mentioned at the start, crude oil flows from the Middle East have substantially rebounded.
turns.zh: 你来过客串很多次了,但这阵子石油话题特别热,所以谢谢你再次做客。——谢谢。正如我开场说的,中东的原油流量已经大幅回升。

turns.en: If I'm not mistaken, they are at or at least close to 20-25 averages at this point, but I'm looking at my screen, oil prices have surged in recent days, again, deep into triple digits.
turns.zh: 如果我没记错的话,现在至少已经接近2025年的均值水平了。但我看着我的屏幕,最近几天油价再度飙升,又一次深入三位数区间。

turns.en: So, what's driving that price move? Yes, so, Brent crude oil prices have risen sharply to now around $112 per barrel because growing tensions in the Middle East and growing downside risks to supply are leading buyers to bidder barrels, both in the physical market and also on the financial side.
turns.zh: 那么,是什么在驱动这轮价格?——是的,Brent(布伦特)原油价格已经大幅上涨到每桶约112美元,因为中东紧张局势升温、供应下行风险加大,买家正在争抢桶油——无论是在现货市场还是金融端。

turns.en: Physical buyers such as refiners are seeing growing downside risks to supply because of an intensification of shipping attacks in the Middle East and because of some strikes on infrastructure by the Houthis and because inventories are low, refiners, physical buyers are trying to get their hands on barrels while they're available because they see a high probability of a sharp drop in supply and on the financial side because bonds and equity
turns.zh: 实物买家,比如炼厂,看到供应下行风险越来越大,因为中东针对航运的袭击在升级,Houthi 也对一些基础设施发动了打击;而且库存很低,炼厂这些实物买家想趁还有货的时候赶紧拿到桶油,因为他们认为供应骤降的概率很高。金融端则是因为债券和股票

turns.en: prices are unusually sensitive to oil prices. There's also a significant bit from investors to hedge their portfolios against energy price upside.
turns.zh: 价格对油价异常敏感,投资者也在大量下单,为组合对冲能源价格上行的风险。

turns.en: Interesting. In some ways, what we're seeing here is precautionary buying by the consumers of crude oil, which makes me think that on the other side of it, that could have price implications.
turns.zh: 有意思。从某种角度看,我们现在看到的是原油消费者的预防性购买(precautionary buying),这让我想到,在另一头,这可能会有价格上的影响。

turns.en: When you think about price risk from here, given these very high levels today and that they're now technically building inventory, what are you expecting and where are the risks skewed?
turns.zh: 在当前这么高的价格水平下,而且库存现在在技术性累积,你怎么看接下来的价格风险?你的预期是什么?风险偏向哪边?

turns.en: Yes, so following the sharp rise in prices, we see the risks to market prices as increasingly metrical, although the risks to our base case price forecast, which sees Brent at the end of this year at 90 and in 2027 annual average at 80, the risks to our forecast are clearly skewed to the upside.
turns.zh: 是的,在价格急涨之后,我们越来越认为市场价格的风险是对称的(symmetric);不过就我们的基准预测而言——今年底 Brent 在90、2027年均价在80——预测的风险明显偏上行。

turns.en: The key upside risks are an intensification of shipping attacks that could lead to a sharp draw in exports, second damage to oil infrastructure, or perhaps a stickier risk premium.
turns.zh: 关键的上行风险包括:航运袭击升级,可能引发出口骤降;其次是石油基础设施受损;或者风险溢价(risk premium)更顽固。

turns.en: Now there's also significant downside risks, especially a potential drop in the risk premium that we estimate at roughly $27 per barrel for Brent at the moment.
turns.zh: 同时也有显著的下行风险,尤其是风险溢价回落——我们估算目前 Brent 的风险溢价大约是每桶27美元。

turns.en: But for the risk premium to come off quickly, you would probably need to see a diplomatic solution that market parties can see as sustainable.
turns.zh: 但风险溢价要快速回落,大概需要看到一个市场各方都认为可持续的外交解决方案。

turns.en: Now, if we don't get significant escalation after the midterms, I think it's reasonable to assume that the risk premium does moderate somewhat.
turns.zh: 如果我们看到中期选举(midterms)之后没有出现重大升级,我认为可以合理假设风险溢价会有所回落。

turns.en: And again, just to be perfectly clear, you said the risk premium is $27 per barrel. So it's a lot of what we have seen in terms of the rise in prices.
turns.zh: 再说得完全清楚一点:你说风险溢价是每桶27美元。这意味着我们看到的涨幅里很大一部分都来自它。

turns.en: So if we did see things improving on the war front, a lot of that could come out. That's right. We think the oil market was balanced last month with oil output equaling demand.
turns.zh: 所以如果战况真的好转,这里面很大一部分可能就会挤出来。——没错。我们认为上个月原油市场是均衡的,产量等于需求。

turns.en: And our fair value estimate of Brent, which is $85 per barrel, does take to account in the inventory levels. And we do think that essentially all of the increase in prices over the last few weeks is driven by an increase in the risk premium rather than an increase in the fair value of Brent.
turns.zh: 而我们 Brent 公允价值的估算——每桶85美元——已经把库存水平考虑在内。我们确实认为过去几周价格的上涨,本质上全部来自风险溢价的扩大,而不是 Brent 公允价值的上升。

turns.en: But it's understandable given the growing downside risk to supply. But it's a different story on the refined product side. We are seeing more physical tightness there.
turns.zh: 但在供应下行风险加大的背景下,这也容易理解。不过成品油那边就是另一个故事了,我们在那里看到更明显的实物趋紧。

turns.en: Tell me about that and what are the implications for product prices that we all consume? Yes, we do estimate that while crude oil exports out of the Persian Gulf are at 100 and 10% of 2025 average levels over the last couple of weeks for refined oil products such as diesel, it's only 40% of 2025 average levels.
turns.zh: 跟我说说成品油这块,以及它对我们所有人消费的产品价格有什么影响?——是的,我们估算,虽然过去几周波斯湾原油出口达到2025年均值的100%到110%,但柴油等成品油的出口只有2025年均值的40%。

turns.en: That's in part because of damage to refineries in the Middle East and also because it's harder to organize these ship-to-ship transfers for refined products than for crude because the products are more inflammable.
turns.zh: 这部分是因为中东炼厂受损,也因为成品油比原油更难组织船对船转运(ship-to-ship)——成品油更易燃。

turns.en: We do think that some of the strength in refined oil product prices such as diesel is not related to the Middle East. You had some significant structural tightness as a result of underinvestment before the war started and Russian refineries have significantly curtailed their outputs of diesel because of the drone attacks from Ukraine.
turns.zh: 我们认为,柴油等成品油价格的强势,有一部分与中东无关。战前就有投资不足造成的结构性紧张;而且由于乌克兰的无人机袭击,俄罗斯炼厂大幅削减了柴油产量。

turns.en: And so even if you were to see a resolution in the Middle East and a significant moderation include prices, we would expect in such a scenario to see diesel prices still well above their historical averages.
turns.zh: 所以,即使中东局势得到解决、油价显著回落,我们预计在那种情景下,柴油价格仍将远高于历史均值。

turns.en: And what about gasoline prices though? Very much in focus here in the US as we look at very high prices at the pump and we are heading into midterm elections.
turns.zh: 那汽油价格呢?在美国这里特别受关注:加油站的油价非常高,而我们正迈向中期选举。

turns.en: What's the outlook there? Yes, so the double negative supply shock from Russia and the Middle East was initially mostly a diesel shock because the Middle East and Russia specialize in refining diesel and they produce heavy barrels that are diesel rich.
turns.zh: 那边前景如何?——是的,来自俄罗斯和中东的双重负面供应冲击,最初主要是柴油冲击,因为中东和俄罗斯专精于炼柴油,他们产出的是富柴油的重质桶。

turns.en: But the tightness in diesel markets is now causing tightness in gasoline markets because when refiners look at the very high diesel margins, they are deciding to switch their output away from gasoline to the higher margin products such as diesel and jet.
turns.zh: 但柴油市场的紧张现在正传导到汽油市场,因为炼厂看到柴油的利润非常高,就决定把产出从汽油转向柴油、航空燃油这些更高利润的产品。

turns.en: And as a result, the gasoline market is tightening very quickly and there's more room for price upside on the gasoline side given a lower starting point for prices and the switching behavior by refiners.
turns.zh: 结果就是汽油市场在快速收紧,考虑到汽油价格起点更低、加上炼厂的切换行为,汽油还有更大的上行空间。

turns.en: More room for upside Dan, that's not good news, but okay, thanks very much for that. The other area that we are seeing substantial price increases is in freight rates in parts of the energy complex.
turns.zh: 上行空间还很大——Daan,这不是好消息,不过好的,非常感谢。另一个我们看到价格大幅上涨的领域,是能源板块部分品种的运费。

turns.en: Why is that happening? Talk us through it. Yeah, so the global average crude freight rate has surged by $20 per barrel over the last year with about three quarters of that increase related to the costs from reorganizing the supply chain to get crude out of the Middle East, both because of a risk premium to compensate the shippers for the higher risk of strikes, but also because we're tying up a lot of tankers
turns.zh: 为什么会这样?给我们讲讲。——好的,全球原油平均运费过去一年飙升了每桶20美元,其中大约四分之三与重组供应链、把原油运出中东的成本有关:既有补偿船东面临更高袭击风险的风险溢价,也是因为大量油轮

turns.en: in an inefficient way via the ship to ship transfers and because the Iranian tankers are also tied up because of the US blockade. The remaining one quarter of the $20 a year price increase reflects higher marine fuel costs.
turns.zh: 被低效地通过船对船转运占用掉了,而且由于美国的封锁,伊朗的油轮也被闲置。这20美元涨幅里剩下的四分之一,反映的是船用燃料成本的上升。

turns.en: The implications are two-fold. It means greater differences in crude prices across regions in places like the Americas, the US, Canada, where crude producers are close to refiners.
turns.zh: 影响有两个层面。其一,意味着各地区原油价差拉大:在美洲——美国、加拿大,产油地离炼厂很近的地方,

turns.en: It means cheaper crude prices in places like Asia, where the refiners are very far away from their crude producers. For instance, the Middle East, they have to pay up the high freight rates and it's putting upward pressure on crude prices and ultimately product prices.
turns.zh: 意味着原油价格更低;而在亚洲这种炼厂离原油产地(比如中东)非常远的地方,他们不得不支付高昂的运费,这给原油价格——最终是产品价格——带来上行压力。

turns.en: The second implication is that ultimately these high freight costs have to be paid mostly by the consumers, and so it's another reason why product prices at the pump, especially in places like Asia, are very elevated.
turns.zh: 第二个影响是,这些高运费最终主要由消费者买单,所以这也是为什么加油站成品油价格——尤其在亚洲等地——如此之高的另一个原因。

turns.en: And that's not impacting, though, freight broadly because it's a very different type of tanker that ships oil, correct? That's right. So the tightness in crude oil tankers is creating some tightness into refined product tankers because you can shift a tanker from a product tanker to a crude tanker, but there are no significant spillovers to broader cargo freight rates for other goods outside of the oil sector.
turns.zh: 不过,这并没有普遍影响整个货运,因为运油的是完全不同类型的船,对吧?——没错。原油油轮的紧张确实会带来成品油轮的一些紧张,因为你可以把成品油轮转去运原油;但对石油行业以外其他货物的广义运费,没有显著的外溢。

turns.en: Let's talk for a moment about European natural gas because LNG, liquefied natural gas, is also being impacted by the war in the Middle East.
turns.zh: 我们聊一会儿欧洲天然气,因为 LNG(liquefied natural gas,液化天然气)同样受到中东战争的影响。

turns.en: If the shipments of LNG remain depressed, as I think they are today, but please give us the lay of the land there, and we have a cold winter in Europe, what are the implications for European energy prices this winter?
turns.zh: 如果 LNG 运输保持低迷——我记得今天还是如此,不过请给我们讲讲现状——而欧洲又迎来一个寒冷的冬天,那今冬欧洲能源价格会怎么样?

turns.en: Yeah, significant upside to energy prices. And while we characterize the risk to market prices for crude as fairly symmetrical, we do see net upside risk to European natural gas prices.
turns.zh: 是的,能源价格有显著的上行。虽然我们形容原油的市场价格风险大致对称,但对欧洲天然气价格,我们确实看到净上行风险。

turns.en: Basically, three reasons. Imageries are very low. It's much harder to store natural gas than it is to store crude. Second to your point, estimated exports of LNG from the Middle East are only at around one-third of 2025 average levels, and in addition to media supply, the second big swing factor is weather.
turns.zh: 基本上三个原因。第一,库存非常低——天然气比原油难储存得多。第二,接着你的话说,我们估计中东的 LNG 出口只有2025年均值的大约三分之一。而且除了供应本身,第二个大摆动因素是天气。

turns.en: And so if we were to see a significant improvement in LNG exports from Qatar, TTF European natural gas prices could decline from roughly 9 euros at the moment to 70.
turns.zh: 所以如果卡塔尔的 LNG 出口大幅改善,欧洲天然气 TTF 价格可能从目前大约90欧元降到70。

turns.en: However, if exports stay at currently low levels, we would see TTF prices in triple digit territory with a potential 70% increase to 150 euros per hour.
turns.zh: 然而,如果出口维持在目前的低位,我们会看到 TTF 价格进入三位数区间——有上涨70%、到每兆瓦时150欧元的可能。

turns.en: If you both get stagnation, low flows from the Middle East, NA1 standard deviation called it an average winter, moreover, this would also spill over into power prices.
turns.zh: 如果两者叠加——中东流量持续低迷,再加上负1个标准差、姑且称之为偏冷的冬天——此外,这还会外溢到电价。

turns.en: And so we see significant upside risk to European energy prices. Just for a little bit more perspective, how does that scenario compare to what we saw in the European energy crisis post the invasion of Ukraine?
turns.zh: 所以我们认为欧洲能源价格存在显著的上行风险。再补充一点背景:这个情景和我们看到的入侵乌克兰之后的欧洲能源危机相比如何?

turns.en: While the size of the shock is roughly comparable, the loss of Russian supply is roughly equal to the loss of Middle East supply today, we would not expect European natural gas prices to rise above 300 euros per megawatt hour, which was the peak in 2022, for a few reasons.
turns.zh: 虽然冲击的规模大致相当——俄罗斯供应的损失与今天中东供应的损失大致相等——但我们不会预期欧洲天然气价格突破每兆瓦时300欧元,那是2022年的峰值,原因有几条。

turns.en: We have lost about 20% of European natural gas demand, and on the supply side, supply outside of the Middle East, including in the US, has risen significantly.
turns.zh: 我们已经失去了大约20%的欧洲天然气需求,而供应端,中东以外的供应——包括美国——大幅上升。

turns.en: So net upside, but not quite the extreme upside from 2022. Understood. So and beyond energy, there are other commodity markets in focus that are tightening.
turns.zh: 所以是净上行,但不是2022年那种极端上行。——明白。那么在能源之外,还有一些大宗商品市场也在收紧。

turns.en: We're focused in particular on copper, what's going on there, and why do you see more tightness ahead? Yeah. So copper prices are up 35% year-over-year.
turns.zh: 我们特别关注铜:那边发生了什么?为什么你认为未来会更紧张?——是的,铜价同比上涨了35%。

turns.en: We see another 10% of upside by the end of next year to 15,600, essentially because the US and China, and this is a broader team across commodity markets, are competing for a limited amount of metal.
turns.zh: 我们预计到明年年底还有10%的上行空间,到15,600,本质上是因为美国和中国——而且这是贯穿整个大宗商品市场更广泛的主题——在争夺有限的金属。

turns.en: The US is importing and stockpiling a lot of copper because of a expectation that there could be US import tariffs on copper. And so traders want to be ahead of the potential tariff, get the metal in now.
turns.zh: 美国在大量进口和囤积铜,因为预期美国可能对铜征收进口关税,所以交易商想在关税落地之前先把金属运进去。

turns.en: And on the Chinese side, there is a big increase in demand for refined copper because of weakness in terms of recycling supply, the supply of recycled scrap copper.
turns.zh: 中国这边,精炼铜需求大增,因为回收供应走弱——也就是再生废铜的供应在减少。

turns.en: So if the two superpowers are pulling on the metal, inventories outside of the US are low, and as those two forces continue to play out, we would expect further tightening and further price upside.
turns.zh: 所以如果两个超级大国都在拉扯这种金属,而美国以外的库存又低,随着这两股力量继续发酵,我们会看到进一步的紧张和进一步的价格上行。

turns.en: And remind us, Dan, what industries consume copper? Who will be feeling the most pain from this upside? Data centers and tech companies, defense companies, electrical equipment companies, car producers, and also producers of solar panels.
turns.zh: Daan,提醒我们一下,哪些行业消耗铜?谁将从这轮涨价里感受到最大的疼痛?——数据中心和科技公司、国防公司、电气设备公司、汽车生产商,还有太阳能板生产商。

turns.en: So it's a fairly widely used commodity, especially for everything related to power, which is precisely a sector where we're seeing a lot of tightness because of the data center power demand.
turns.zh: 所以它是一种用途相当广泛的大宗商品,尤其是一切与电力相关的领域——而这恰恰是我们看到大量紧张局面的板块,因为数据中心带来的电力需求。

turns.en: So more reason for some cost inflation there. The other commodity I wanted to ask you about, Dan, to close out, is gold. Generally, we see downward pressure on gold when interest rates are elevated.
turns.zh: 这意味着那里的成本通胀又多了几分理由。Daan,最后我想问你的另一种大宗商品是黄金。一般来说,利率高企时我们会看到黄金承压。

turns.en: We know that we have been in a higher rate environment in the recent period, but you're still pretty bullish on gold. So talk us through why you think gold has some resilience here.
turns.zh: 我们知道最近一段时间一直处于较高的利率环境,但你对黄金仍然相当看好。讲讲你为什么认为黄金在这里有一些韧性。

turns.en: I think the structural bull factor for the gold outlook has not changed. If you, for instance, look at the last three months, central banks have been buying at a base that's 5x the pre-2022 average when Russia's reserves got frozen.
turns.zh: 我认为黄金前景的结构性看多因素并没有改变。比如,看过去三个月,央行的购金速度是2022年之前平均水平的5倍——就是俄罗斯储备被冻结的那个时点之前。

turns.en: Now on the cyclical side, the increase in rates does pose a challenge to investor gold demand and to gold prices. But in the base case of our economists, the Fed is done hiking after a last hike in December, and because some of the rate hikes are priced in, we do see a significant upside to gold prices in our base case because of central bank buying and an improvement in the rates environment.
turns.zh: 现在在周期性层面,利率上升确实对投资者的黄金需求和金价构成挑战。但在我们经济学家的基准情景里,美联储在12月完成最后一次加息后就停止加息,而且部分加息已经被定价,所以在基准情景下,由于央行购金和利率环境的改善,我们看到金价有显著的上行空间。

turns.en: Thanks again for joining us, Dan. Appreciate it. Thank you, Allison. This episode of Goldman Sachs Exchanges was recorded on Thursday, October 22nd, 2026.
turns.zh: 再次感谢你的加入,Daan。很感激。——谢谢你,Allison。本集 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 录制于2026年10月22日,星期四。
